html:
The Rogun Dam is a hydroelectric dam on the Vakhsh River in central Tajikistan, begun in Soviet times in 1976 and restarted after independence. Its first turbine began work in 2018.

When finished it is planned to be the tallest dam in the world, at about 335 metres, upstream of the older Nurek Dam. Work stopped when the Soviet Union fell and during the civil war. President Emomali Rahmon made it a national cause, and families were pushed to buy shares.

Uzbekistan, downstream, long opposed it, fearing for the water of its cotton fields on the Amu Darya, which feeds the Aral Sea. Relations eased after 2016. Tajikistan hopes to sell its power to Afghanistan and Pakistan.
sum: The Rogun Dam is a hydroelectric dam on the Vakhsh River in central Tajikistan, begun in Soviet times in 1976 and restarted after independence. Its first turbine began work in 2018.
